title: Functorial Cech total complexes and augmentations for arbitrary module complexes
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme], a family $U=(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of open subsets, and a complex $K^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules in degrees $\mathbf N$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], apply the coefficient Cech functor [def-sc-module-cech-comparison] termwise and totalize. Restrictions of global sections into the $(n,0)$ summands give a cochain map $\alpha_K:\Gamma(X,K^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Tot}\check C(U,K^\bullet)$. A module map $a:F\to K^0$ satisfying $a d_K=0$ gives a cochain map $\beta_a:\check C(U,F)\to\operatorname{Tot}\check C(U,K^\bullet)$ into the $(0,n)$ summands. These maps are natural under coefficient cochain maps (for beta, provided the augmentations commute), and specialize definitionally to the existing resolution maps $\alpha$ and $\beta$. The double functor packages the existing termwise functor rather than defining another Cech object.

proof.text: Apply the additive Cech functor termwise, and compose with the existing first-quadrant total functor. Define alpha and beta components by restrictions and coefficient augmentation followed by the corresponding total summand inclusions.

Use moduleCechZero_d and moduleCechZero_naturality for the alpha cochain equation. For beta, the resolution-direction differential is zero by a d=0, and Cech naturality proves the other direction. The total signs are 1 on the beta axis.

The total-map equation on summand inclusions reduces alpha naturality to moduleCechZero_naturality and beta naturality to functoriality and the augmentation equation. Specialization to existing injective-resolution maps is reflexivity.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including InjectiveResolution.desc_commutes and Hom.ι_comp_hom. No arbitrary-complex Cech augmentation or pushed-forward tuple-total naturality theorem.
Twelve ShortComplex results about preservation of homology and componentwise isomorphisms. No Cech refinement theorem.

Mathlib refinement matches concern Stone-Cech compactification. Library ModuleCechLiftSquares proves squares only for two injective resolutions. cupCechDouble gives the same termwise object but no arbitrary-complex augmentation API. FirstQuadrantTotalComparison gives total comparison, not sectionwise acyclicity or refinement. Blueprint search for Cech refinement, Cech quasi-isomorphism and 01FD gives no imported blueprint node.
